title: Unexpected Reinforcement
next_chapter_hook: The characters on the secret letter were ancient and yellowed, yet they cut into Chen Ji's eyes like blades—a name he had never heard, yet intimately connected to the ultimate secret of the Tianji Record.

text.content:
The lantern light flickered, casting long shadows in the damp passage. Chen Ji's hand was already on his sword hilt, his knuckles faintly white—a rare loss of composure for him. His father's dying words still echoed in his ears; the murderer was among the Five Elders, yet the one approaching was Su Qingyao.

She wore dust-covered blue robes, her hair slightly disheveled, nothing like her usual dignified appearance as the Inner Sect Senior Fellow of Tianqing Sect. But those clear, cold eyes were brighter than ever under the candlelight.

"Why are you here?" Chen Ji's voice was extremely low, yet his sword intent had quietly receded. He stared at Su Qingyao, his gaze sweeping over her—no wounds, no bloodstains, only a kind of... exhaustion he had never seen before.

Su Qingyao did not answer immediately. She walked closer step by step, each footstep pressing on Chen Ji's taut nerves. Only when she was within three feet did she stop, taking a yellowed letter from her embrace.

"Chen Ji," her voice was somewhat hoarse, "your father's legacy shouldn't remain only within the illusion of the Tianji Record."

Chen Ji's pupils constricted sharply. His hand left the sword hilt but froze mid-air, as if held by some invisible force.

"How did you..."

"How did I know about the things your father left behind?" Su Qingyao smiled lightly, her smile carrying no mockery, only an inexplicable bitterness, "Because fifteen years ago, he saved my life."

dialogue.content: "Fifteen years ago, I was an orphan left to die in the snow." Su Qingyao lowered her eyes, her lashes casting faint shadows on her cheeks, "If Uncle Chen hadn't passed by, I would have long become a pile of yellow earth."
Chen Ji was silent for a moment, then slowly spoke: "I never knew my father had such past events." His tone was calm, yet something churned in his chest, "So you came here..."

"To repay a debt of gratitude." Su Qingyao raised her head, meeting Chen Ji's scrutinizing gaze directly, "And to investigate. Three months ago, I accidentally discovered the aura of the Tianji Record appearing in the Outer Disciple/Servant quarters. I traced it for three months and finally confirmed it was you."

text.content:
Three months. Chen Ji's heart tightened. During these three months, he thought he had hidden without a trace, yet unaware that a pair of eyes had been watching him from the shadows. What surprised him even more was that the owner of these eyes was not an enemy, but...

"You've been testing me all along." Not a question, but a statement.

Su Qingyao nodded, frank to the point of being cold: "Three times. Each time you perfectly resolved the crisis—that's not something atrash can do." Her lips curved slightly upward, "Playing the pig to eat the tiger, you're very good at it."

dialogue.content: "Since you've already seen through everything," Chen Ji's voice was low, "why didn't you expose me?" He stared at Su Qingyao, "If one of the Five Elders really killed my father, getting too close to me—you're not afraid of bringing trouble upon yourself?"

Su Qingyao did not answer. She simply extended the letter in her hand forward.

"This is what I owe Uncle Chen." Her voice softened, "When he saved me back then, he left a letter, saying it was for his descendants. I've kept it all these years, originally intending to personally deliver it to the Chen family's descendants, but I learned the Chen family had suffered misfortune..."

text.content:
The moment Chen Ji took the letter, his fingers actually trembled slightly. This was something his father left behind—the real, tangible legacy, not the fleeting illusion within the Tianji Record.

He took a deep breath, suppressing the churning emotions in his heart.

"I owe you a favor."

Su Qingyao shook her head: "No, your father saved me once, I repaid his descendants once—it's only natural." Her gaze fell on the letter in Chen Ji's hand, "But the things within the letter... you should be mentally prepared."

choice.prompt: Su Qingyao reminds that the contents of the letter require mental preparation. How do you respond?

choices.text: Open the letter in front of her
choices.description: Since she accompanied you here, there's nothing to hide. Opening it in front of her also demonstrates trust.
choices.risk_hint: If the letter contains content one doesn't want others to know, it may lead to a passive position

text.content:
Chen Ji did not hesitate. He opened the seal in front of Su Qingyao. The paper was old but well-preserved. The moment he unfolded it, a faint scent of ink rushed toward him—that was the pine soot ink his father always used.

Familiar handwriting entered Chen Ji's eyes, and his hands trembled again.

"Ji'er, if you can see this letter, it means your father is no longer among the living..."

dialogue.content:
Su Qingyao stood quietly to the side, her gaze without prying, only waiting. She had seen too many people lose composure when facing relics of their loved ones, and at this moment, she chose to give Chen Ji space.

"I'll go guard the passage entrance first." She said softly, "Some things shouldn't have a third pair of eyes."

choices.description: Your father's affairs shouldn't be enjoyed alone, and since she has kept this letter for many years, she also has the right to know. Witnessing together also means bearing together.
choices.risk_hint: If the letter's contents involve core secrets of the Tianji Record, the fates of both will be more closely bound

text.content:
"No need." Chen Ji shook his head, "Since you've kept this for many years, you're also a party involved."

He opened the seal in front of Su Qingyao. The paper was old but well-preserved. The moment he unfolded it, a faint scent of ink rushed toward him—that was the pine soot ink his father always used.

Familiar handwriting entered Chen Ji's eyes, and his hands trembled again.

"Ji'er, if you can see this letter, it means your father is no longer among the living..."

dialogue.content:
Su Qingyao's figure stiffened slightly, then she walked to Chen Ji's side, standing shoulder to shoulder with him. Candlelight flickered between the two, casting their shadows on the mottled stone walls, giving them an air of depending on each other for survival.

"...I'll accompany you." Her voice was very soft, yet exceptionally firm.

choices.description: The things my father left me, I want to face them alone first. I'll then inform her of the key points.
choices.risk_hint: Su Qingyao may think you still have reservations about her

text.content:
"Give me a moment."

Chen Ji turned around, his back to Su Qingyao, and opened the envelope alone. His back view seemed somewhat lonely under the candlelight, yet also revealed an indomitable determination.

Su Qingyao did not speak, only quietly stepping back two paces, giving him space.

"...Ji'er, if you can see this letter, it means your father is no longer among the living..."

The handwriting on the letter was bold and powerful, consistent with his father's style. Chen Ji read line by line, his brow furrowing tighter and tighter.

"The Tianji Record was not granted by the Heavens, but left behind by an ancient great one who risked their life. All past holders met untimely ends. Your father observed its fragments for over ten years and deeply knows it harbors a catastrophic calamity..."

"Remember: Do not let the Tianji Record become complete. When fragmented, the backlash can still be withstood; if all parts are gathered, divine punishment will surely follow, and the holder will become abandoned by the Heavens..."

Chen Ji's pupils violently constricted. The truth of the Tianji Record—his father actually already knew?

He continued reading, his fingers unconsciously gripping the edge of the paper tighter.

"Your father's entire life was fraught with misfortune, all because of the Tianji Record. If one day you also obtain this object, I hope you remember: protect it, but do not pursue its completeness. Your father has left a contingency for you..."

"Contingency?" Chen Ji murmured to himself.

"At the end of the letter," Su Qingyao's voice came from behind him, gentle yet clear, "Uncle Chen also left a message for me, asking me to personally relay it to his descendant."

dialogue.content:
Su Qingyao took a deep breath, her voice slightly trembling:

"Uncle Chen said—'If Ji'er is determined to walk that path one day, tell him this: the Eye of Heaven never sleeps.'"

The Eye of Heaven!

These four words were like a thunderbolt striking Chen Ji's mind. The final BOSS of Volume Eight of the Tianji Record, that transcendent consciousness—his father actually knew of its existence long ago?

text.content:
Chen Ji spun around, staring at Su Qingyao intently.

"Are you certain these are exactly the four words?"

Su Qingyao nodded, her gaze without any evasion: "After Uncle Chen said these words back then, his expression was extremely complicated. He said this was the only thing he could do for his descendants—lighting a lamp for him in the darkness, even if only a little."

Chen Ji closed his eyes, his mind racing. His father's meaning was clear—he knew the complete truth of the Tianji Record, even knew of the Eye of Heaven's existence. But he didn't stop his descendants from inheriting the Tianji Record; instead, he chose another way...

Leaving a lamp.

choice.prompt: After learning his father's dying words, Chen Ji needs to respond

choices.text: Make a blood oath of vengeance with her
choices.description: She kept this letter for fifteen years and investigated you for three months. Now that the truth is revealed, you're on the same boat.
choices.visible_reward: Su Qingyao becomes an official ally, unlocking the "Joint Investigation" storyline
choices.risk_hint: The fates of both will be more closely bound; once they fail, it's mutual destruction

text.content:
Chen Ji opened his eyes, his gaze gaining a solemnity never seen before.

"Su Qingyao." He looked directly into her eyes, "You investigated me for three months, kept this letter for fifteen years, and now followed me to the depths of this ruins..."

He paused, his voice low yet firm:

"I, Chen Ji, today make a pact with you—the blood feud of patricide is unforgivable. Regardless of who the murderer is, regardless of who stands behind them, I will make them pay in blood."

"Will you stand shoulder to shoulder with me?"

dialogue.content:
Su Qingyao met Chen Ji's gaze, her eyes slightly reddened. Fifteen years of waiting, fifteen years of guarding—this finally had a response.

"I, Su Qingyao, today make a pact with Chen Ji—the grace of Uncle Chen, I shall repay in the next life; but his仇, I will take revenge together with you."

The two clasped hands tightly, and under the flickering candlelight, made the heaviest vow of their lives.

"From now on, your affairs are my affairs." Su Qingyao said softly, "Be it through fire or over swords."

choices.description: She knows far too much. You need to confirm whether she's purely repaying a debt of gratitude or has ulterior motives.
choices.visible_reward: Gain more information and understand Su Qingyao's complete motivation
choices.risk_hint: May make Su Qingyao feel questioned, delaying relationship development

text.content:
"Wait." Chen Ji did not release the letter in his hand, his gaze sharp, "You know far more than this."

Su Qingyao was slightly stunned but did not avoid his gaze.

"How can you track this ruins? How do you know the weight of this letter? Do you have connections with some among the Five Elders?"

Chen Ji's voice was calm, yet pressed step by step. This was his usual caution—before extending trust, he must confirm the other party hides no blade.

dialogue.content:
Su Qingyao was silent for a moment, then smiled lightly.

"You are indeed Uncle Chen's son." Her smile carried a trace of bitterness, "In his testament letter, there was a sentence—'If there's a Ji'er, remember not to let him trust others easily. His suspicious nature is precisely why he can survive until the end.'"

She paused, continuing: "The reason I could track this place is because three months ago, the aura of the Tianji Record suddenly intensified. And that coincided precisely with the time you began cultivating the Tianji Record fragments."

text.content:
Just then, the content on the last page of the letter entered Chen Ji's sight.

That line of handwriting was noticeably different from the rest—more hurried, more urgent, as if his father had hastily written it under extreme urgency.

"Ji'er, there's one more thing. Your father once glimpsed a corner of the future from the Tianji Record—our Chen bloodline will have a 'Heavenly Fate Lock Key' emerge. This person concerns the only variable after the Tianji Record becomes complete."

Chen Ji's mind exploded. Heavenly Fate Lock Key—his father actually knew of Chen Nian's existence long ago?

"Chen Ji?" Su Qingyao sensed his unusual state and frowned, "What does the letter say?"

Chen Ji did not answer. His gaze was fixed on that line, his heart pounding like a war drum.

"If this person falls into the Holy Sect's hands, the completion of the Tianji Record will become meaningless."

Chen Nian.

His sister who had been missing for years. The person he had been searching for all along.

His father actually knew of her importance long ago, yet never mentioned a single word to him.

How many more secrets... are hidden here?

Deep within the ruins, candlelight flickered. Chen Ji held his father's testament letter, speechless for a long time.

Su Qingyao stood beside him, not pressing for answers. She simply waited quietly, just as she had waited in the snow fifteen years ago for Uncle Chen's rescue—only that time, she waited for life, but now...

Looking at Chen Ji's tense back, a strange bitterness welled up in her heart.

This man carries far more weight on his shoulders than she ever imagined.

"Chen Ji." She spoke softly, "Whatever the letter says, you don't have to bear it alone."

Chen Ji slowly turned around. In his gaze toward her, for the first time, there was a trace of genuine gratitude.

"...Thank you."

He drew out an insert page from within the letter. On it was written only one name.

The handwriting was unfamiliar, yet carried a strange sense of familiarity.

"Lu Chenyuan."

This name, Chen Ji had never seen in any classical text, nor in the records of the three major sects. But for some reason, looking at these three characters, his heart suddenly tightened—

As if this name itself carried some power sufficient to overturn everything.

"Who is this person?" Chen Ji asked quietly, "Why did Father write his name separately in this letter?"

Su Qingyao leaned in to glance, her brow furrowing: "This name... I seem to have heard it somewhere before, but I can't recall for the moment."

Outside the ruins, the wind howled. Chen Ji carefully put away the letter, raised his eyes to look into the darkness of the deep passage.

The answer, perhaps, lies ahead.

And their path of revenge has just begun.

"Let's go." He said softly, "Among the Five Elders, there must be the murderer. We... should return."

dialogue.content:
Su Qingyao nodded and walked toward the passage exit shoulder to shoulder with him.

As they passed a broken stone tablet, Chen Ji's peripheral vision suddenly caught sight of several ancient characters carved on it: "Heavenly Secrets... do not... gaze upon..."

His footsteps paused slightly, then he continued forward without letting Su Qingyao notice his unusual state.

Father was right. The secrets of the Tianji Record run far deeper than he imagined. And that name—Lu Chenyuan—regardless of who this person is, they are inevitably connected to all of this by countless threads.

Chen Ji gripped the letter in his embrace tighter, his gaze gradually cooling.

"Someday, I will dig out all the truth." He silently vowed in his heart, "No matter the cost."
